decisions.statement: Pitch surface carries 25 distinct pitch positions: each row 12 equal-width keys (C3..B3 and C4..B4) plus one standalone C5 key (channel 24) at the top-right of the upper row. The top position is NOT duplicated across the two rows. This confirms specification v2.0 section 2 and makes the carrier board's 26 groups the outlier, not the spec.

facts.pitch_electrodes: 73 if C5 is a single pad (spec line 22) or 75 if C5 gets 3 electrodes - UNRESOLVED
facts.electrode_budget: 84 total; both 73+5+6 and 75+5+4 close the account

evidence.authority: Direct human WorkBuddy user_query, corroborated in-repo by docs/02-技术方案/25-音高与八度规格.md section 2 lines 20-22 and 29-30

hardware_impact.action_required: Drop one top group (3 electrodes) per row before fabrication. Zero cost while un-fabricated; a re-spin if changed after fabrication.

decisions.note: User's derivation '26 = 12+12+2 high positions' was not established by the evidence, but the decision it led to (no duplicated top endpoint) matches specification v2.0 section 2 verbatim, which also supplies the technical reason: two adjacent keys on the same pitch double-trigger at the boundary and burn two voices plus two note-offs. The companion claim that the 16 digital bits are 8 harmonics plus 5 octave cells is rejected: the 16 bits are 8 harmonics + 4 presets + 1 edit + 3 encoder, and the 5 octave cells are on the analog side. Open: whether channel 24 uses 1 or 3 electrodes, which sets the pitch electrode total at 73 or 75.
